title: Normalized ordinary pullback comparison on represented charts
statement: Fix a prime ell, a finite extension E/Q_ell, schemes T,S, a morphism g:T → S and a pro-etale object U over S [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let V be its base change and v:V.left → U.left. Use completed coefficient sheaves [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], projection-defined structural maps and the constant-section/projection normalized chart ring isomorphisms [lem-tw-completed-coefficient-ringed-coherence]. Write r_U,r_V for sectionwise chart restrictions with those coefficient identifications, P_g,P_v for ordinary module pullbacks and D_g,D_v their specified right adjoints [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. There is an isomorphism beta:D_g;r_U ≅ r_V;D_v whose component on H and m is restriction of m along the canonical fibre-product isomorphism H ×_U V ≅ H ×_S T. There is an isomorphism lambda:r_U;P_v ≅ P_g;r_V, and lambda_M equals P_v(r_U(eta_g,M)) followed by P_v(beta_(P_g M)) and epsilon_v,(r_V(P_g M)). All universes of schemes and coefficients are independent. No derived functors are part of this statement.

proof.text: The represented slice equivalences identify the over-sites at U,V with the pro-etale sites of U.left,V.left. The coefficient isomorphisms supplied by completedRingMap_slice are independent of the auxiliary morphism: constant-sheaf maps are determined by their constant-section equations, and completed-ring maps are determined by all finite projections. Thus they are exactly chartRingIso. Coefficient coherence identifies the restricted structural map with the completedRingMap of v.

source.place: Tag 04J0, localization of module pullback; Tags 04IF and 03CE

proof.text: Localize the ordinary module adjunction at U. The finite-product comparison for pro-etale base change identifies the localized module right adjoints. The coefficient equality in step 1 makes this a linear comparison after transport through the represented slice equivalences. Its section map on H is restriction along completedRingSlicePointIso, and its inverse is induced by the inverse point isomorphism. The localized pullback comparison is invertible by the module localization theorem. Its adjunct is restriction of the global unit followed by beta. Inverse adjunction gives the stated unit/beta/counit formula. Site and coefficient equivalences preserve the formula by their unit equations.
